policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Read the required quantities and colors from the goal at every step; unrequested colors have quota zero. First update the deposit counters from the observed execution interval. All supplied episodes start in A with an empty hand and counters zero. Apply these rules to the current situation rather than advancing a stored phase: if all requested quotas are satisfied, choose C, press the button, even if more cubes remain visible. Otherwise, if a requested cube is currently held, choose B, put it into the bin. A successful A therefore leads to B; a completed B leads to C if the updated counters meet every quota, and otherwise to A. If the hand is empty and a quota remains, choose A targeting a visible free cube of a still-needed color. For mixed goals, select the next needed color according to the goal's quotas: for three blue and two green, complete green before blue; for two red and three green, complete green before red; for two red and one green, complete red before green. For the previously covered mixed red-and-green layout with the bin near [130, 117], retain green before red. These priorities govern A with an empty hand, not B for a cube already held. The instruction does not specify an ordering among same-color cubes; to reproduce the supplied choices use these scene-conditioned tie-breaks, matching approximate locations to current visible objects rather than requiring exact pixel equality: for two blue cubes with the bin near [123, 141], select the cube near [86, 136] when blue_deposited is zero and near [86, 88] when it is one. For three red cubes with the bin near [110, 130], select near [67, 157], [115, 189], or [71, 137] when red_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two. For three blue cubes with the bin near [91, 111], select near [96, 82], [67, 115], or [117, 106] when blue_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two. For the mixed goal with the bin near [130, 117], select green near [80, 91], [105, 116], or [106, 162] when green_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two; after three green deposits select red near [63, 84]. For the one-green goal select the initially visible green cube near [81, 153]. Additional target preferences apply only when both the goal and layout match: for three blue and two green with the bin near [90, 148], select green near [99, 82] or [118, 81] when green_deposited is respectively zero or one; after completing the green quota, select blue near [61, 171], [112, 152], or [88, 184] when blue_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two. For one red with the bin near [112, 177], select red near [79, 127]. For two red and three green with the bin near [94, 155], select green near [68, 178], [71, 75], or [90, 181] when green_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two; after completing the green quota, select red near [54, 99] or [100, 121] when red_deposited is respectively zero or one. For two blue with the bin near [122, 181], select blue near [91, 163] or [97, 117] when blue_deposited is respectively zero or one. For two red and one green with the bin near [107, 86], select red near [74, 98] or [64, 83] when red_deposited is respectively zero or one; after completing the red quota, select green near [105, 117]. Match these approximate locations to current visible free cubes of the selected color; use the fallback if a preferred candidate is absent. Output A's point within the selected cube, in [y, x] order, using its current visible position. B and C need no point. For an unfamiliar layout or absent preferred candidate, choose another visible free cube of a needed color, breaking ties by smallest y then smallest x. A failed grasp with an empty hand leads to another A, without incrementing any counter. If a needed cube is temporarily occluded, use its latest clearly observed location in the current interval. If no needed candidate is observable anywhere in that interval, make a best-effort A at the most plausible accessible location rather than falsely declaring completion; preserve counters unless a deposit is actually observed.

fields.name: blue_deposited
fields.description: Initialize to zero if incoming memory is empty. Otherwise start from the incoming integer. Scan the supplied execution frames for a blue cube carried by the gripper toward the bin and released there, followed by an empty, opening or open gripper withdrawing and the cube disappearing inside the opaque bin. Increment once per such completed deposit in this interval. Use the held cube's color before release; do not count pickup, issuing B, repeated post-release frames, or unrelated cubes appearing or disappearing. Elevated wrist coordinates need not equal the bin's visible center. Preserve if no blue deposit is observed. e.g. 1
